description: The characterization checklist: what a characterization of an engine records, area by area. Each item is an option of the loose core (docs/core-semantics.md, the option catalogue; kind `option`) or a point the options do not reach (kind `extra`). A fact names the items it settles in its `options` field, and `python -m sverify_dev.facts --coverage <engine>` lists, per item, the engine's facts that settle it, or `missing`.

Item ids are unique across areas, so each option sits in one area even where it applies to functions of several (`overflow` covers integer `sum` too). The option ids are the catalogue's for now; once #444's step 1a lands, they will come from Lean's options table (`SubstraitLean/Options.lean`), and a test will check the two agree.

items.question: `+ - ×`, negate, `abs`, `MIN / -1` and integer `sum` past the declared width: raise, wrap or saturate, at which width.
Integer `modulus` (and `divide`): truncated or floored.
A zero divisor of integers and of doubles: error, NULL, IEEE or a limit.
`MIN % -1`: 0 or a raise.
Shifts by a negative count or by the width or more, and bits shifted out.
A result with more digits than its scale: how it rounds.
The precision and scale of decimal arithmetic and aggregates, and overflow past 38 digits.
Rounding of arithmetic and of `round` (to `d` digits too).
`sqrt`, logs, `asin`, `acos`, `atan2`, `power` outside their domain: NaN, NULL or a raise.
A logarithm of zero: -inf, NaN or a raise.
`inf - inf`, `0 · inf`, `inf / inf`, `fmod(inf, y)`, a sum of both infinities: NaN or a raise.
Is NaN equal to NaN in `=`, grouping, `DISTINCT` and joins.
Where NaN sorts, and how `MIN`, `MAX`, `<`, `greatest` treat it.
Does a NaN's sign (or payload) survive and show.
`-0.0` in arithmetic, comparison, sorting and grouping.
Single-precision arithmetic and its conversions.
`upper`, `lower`: Unicode or ASCII mappings.
`like`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `strpos`, regexes: case-sensitive or not.
`substring` offsets and lengths outside 32 bits.
`substring` with a negative or zero start; its indexing (characters or bytes, 0- or 1-based).
The regex engine and syntax, classes on non-ASCII text, a match that fails, replacement references.
`md5`, `sha256` and other digests: present, and on which bytes.
Date and timestamp arithmetic past 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31.
`TIME ± INTERVAL` with months, and time arithmetic past midnight.
The timestamp unit (s, ms, µs, ns) and its range.
Time zones: DST gaps and overlaps, conversions.
Week numbers, weekdays, ISO years, `date_trunc` to a week, parts before 1970.
A double or decimal cast to an integer: truncate or round.
A cast that does not fit or parse: raise or NULL.
Text to numbers, booleans and dates: what is accepted (spaces, signs, `nan`, `inf`, exponents).
Numbers, booleans and dates to text: the format.
`concat` and other functions given a NULL: NULL or skip.
`and`, `or`, `not` with NULLs; `bool_and`, `bool_or` over NULLs.
Do NULL keys match in joins, and how `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` is spelled.
A NULL element deciding `<` of lists, in comparisons and in `ORDER BY`.
List indexing: base, negative and out-of-range indexes.
Equality and order of structs with NULL fields.
UNNEST of a NULL list and of an empty one.
`avg` of integers: its type and how it is computed.
The order and grouping of a double `SUM`, `AVG`.
The algorithm of `VAR_*`, `STDDEV_*`, `COVAR_*`, `CORR`.
`CORR` of one pair or a constant side; a statistical aggregate of a single value.
`QUANTILE_CONT`, `QUANTILE_DISC`, `MEDIAN`: the position and interpolation.
Which row `FIRST`, `LAST`, `ARG_MIN`, `ARG_MAX`, `any_value`, `MODE` take among ties.
Aggregates of no rows or of NULLs only (`SUM`, `COUNT`, `MIN`, `AVG`).
Aggregates of ±inf and NaN inputs.
How `NTILE` spreads the remainder.
The frame when none is given, with and without an order; rank functions over ties and NULLs.
The order of ties in a sort, `STRING_AGG`, `collect`, a window: stable or not.
Where NULLs sort by default, ascending and descending.
A sort that only clusters equal keys.
`UNION`, `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT`, with and without `ALL`: duplicates, NULLs, order.
Grouping, `DISTINCT` and join keys with NaN and `-0.0`: one group, and which value represents it.
Where the engine raises beyond the reference (D2): extra raises, and raises that are planning errors or panics.
The engine's names of the types.
Implicit casts and type promotion in arithmetic and comparisons.
The types of literals.
File formats read and written, and their type mappings.
Object stores and their credentials.
Catalogs (Unity, Iceberg, …) and how the engine attaches them.
